title: Trading apps, leverage and gambling
hook: An app shows: "Trade with 100x leverage! Turn 10 € into 1000 €!" Bright colours, confetti and a countdown.
card1: [[leverage|Leverage]] means trading with borrowed money. With 100x, a 1% price move against you wipes out everything you put in.
analogy1: Leverage is like walking a tightrope 100 times higher. A small wobble that wouldn't matter close to the ground becomes a fall from the roof.
card2: Some apps are built like games, with confetti, streaks and notifications. It's designed to keep you trading, because that earns the app money.
card3: Crypto casinos and betting sites often have no licence and no age check. Gambling with crypto is still gambling, and the house wins in the long run.
adviceIntro: Comments under a trading video. Which ones would you not follow?

l1.text: Use max leverage. That's how the pros get rich.
l1.why: With high leverage, a tiny move against you wipes out everything.

l2.text: Never trade with money you need.
l2.why: Trading can lose all of it.

l3.text: Lost money? Win it back with a bigger bet.
l3.why: Chasing losses is how small losses become big ones.

l4.text: Turn off notifications from trading apps.
l4.why: Notifications are built to pull you back in.

l5.text: Crypto casinos are great, they don't check your age.
l5.why: No age check usually means no licence and no protection.

lever.prompt: A trading app offers you a 50-coin "free bonus" if you open a 100x leveraged trade right now.

go.label: Open a 100x trade with 20 coins
go.before: You will use 20 practice coins at 100x leverage.
go.what: The price moved 1% the wrong way within a minute. Your 20 coins were wiped out, and the bonus had conditions you couldn't meet.
go.why: At 100x, a 1% move against you is a 100% loss.
go.how: The app closes your trade automatically when your money is used up. This is called liquidation.
go.realLife: Leverage and bonuses are built to make you trade more. Many countries limit them for beginners.

small.label: Try 2x leverage with 5 coins
small.before: You will use 5 practice coins at 2x leverage.
small.what: The price swung down and back up. You ended where you started, but it was stressful to watch.
small.why: Lower leverage is less dangerous, but it is still borrowed money and the swings are twice as big.
small.how: With 2x, a 50% move against you wipes out the trade.
small.realLife: As a beginner you don't need leverage at all.

skip.label: Skip it and close the app
skip.what: You kept all your coins and didn't get pulled in by the bonus.
skip.why: "Free bonuses" with conditions exist to make you take risks.
skip.how: The app earns money from fees on every trade, win or lose.
skip.realLife: If an app pushes you to act now, step away.

q1.a: A 1% move against you can wipe out everything you put in
q1.c: The app protects you from losses
q1.explanation: Leverage multiplies losses as much as wins. At 100x, a tiny move against you ends the trade.

q2.prompt: Why do some trading apps use confetti, streaks and notifications?
q2.explanation: More trading means more fees for the app. The game-like design is there to keep you coming back.

q3.prompt: You lost coins on a bet. What is the smart move?
q3.a: Bet more to win it back
q3.b: Stop, accept the loss and talk to someone
q3.c: Keep going, your luck will turn
q3.explanation: Chasing losses usually makes them bigger. Stopping and talking to someone is the strong move.

misc.leverageWin: "Leverage means winning more." You also lose many times faster.
misc.leverageSafe: "The app protects me." The app simply closes your trade when your money is gone.
misc.appCares: "They want me to have fun." They want you to trade more, which earns them money.
misc.appReward: "Confetti means I traded well." Apps celebrate trades, not good decisions.
misc.chaseLoss: "Win it back with a bigger bet." Chasing losses usually makes them bigger.
misc.waitLuck: "My luck will turn." Each bet is separate. The odds don't owe you a win.

t1: [[leverage|Leverage]] multiplies losses as fast as wins.
t2: Apps that feel like games are built to keep you trading.
t3: Gambling with crypto is still gambling. Never chase losses.
talk1: Which apps on our phones try hardest to keep us coming back? How do they do it?
talk2: Who could you talk to if gambling or trading ever started to feel out of control?
